text:
Maya: Quick follow-up on the precision profiles RFC — thinking we should expose a per-model 'precision_profile' (server-side, part of model metadata) rather than a per-request flag. Keeps hot path simple and lets us do smarter kernel selection. Thoughts?

Vikram: +1 to model-level profiles. Per-request flags explode scheduler complexity and make batching hard. Can we support per-route overrides for a few trusted partners though?

Maya: yeah per-route overrides but only if the route is pinned to a dedicated capacity pool. Otherwise no.

Jenn: Main question: how do we guard quality? If a profile switches to FP8 or 4-bit, we need automatic evals + rollback. Suggest mandatory eval suite per model version: perf (p95 latency), and quality (task-specific eval set).

Diego: Agree. Also want this to plug into Redwood Optimize so model owners get suggestions (e.g., use int8 for chat-worst-case but fp8 for long-form). Could we emit a "profile_recommendation" signal from offline runs?

Vikram: Implementation note: runtime should present a small surface: profile hint + fallback chain. Example config:

```
precision_profile:
  name: "balanced-small"
  tiers: ["fp8", "int8", "int4"]
  fallback_policy: "degrade_to=int8"
  max_tail_latency_ms: 120
```

Scheduler only needs tiers and max_tail_latency. Everything else is evaluative metadata.

Jenn: +codeblock. For quality gates: offline eval thresholds and continuous monitoring. Metrics to track: eval_perplexity_delta, exact_match_drop_pct, topk_nll_shift. Rollout if all < thresholds. If any breach -> automatic canary pause + notify.

Maya: How about KV cache and attention keys? Changing precision can break cache compatibility across workers. We need an invariant: cached KV blobs must include profile version. If profile changes during rollout, invalidate prefix caches or ensure hot-path fallback doesn't mix precisions.

Vikram: Good catch. Implementation approach: stash KV with header {model_version, profile_hash}. On lookup, require match; otherwise simulate a cache miss. Costly but safe. Might need a fast path: allow int8 and fp8 compatible cache representation for specific kernels, but that's an optimization later.

Diego: Ops questions: do we allow mixed-precision inside a layer (layer-wise quant)? If we do, the profile becomes a per-layer map which complicates storage. Maybe v1 keep profile as global per-weight quantization with optional layer overrides for a handful of layers (LLM-head, QKV).

Jenn: For rollout strategy: canary 1% for 2h with full eval runs, 5% for 6h, then 25/50/100. Run continuous quality probes using the eval set + live-sampled user prompts with privacy-safe hashing.

Maya: SRE concerns?

SRE-Bot: Deploy pipeline note: if a profile change requires kernel switch, node draining will trigger re-kernelization; expect ~20-45s of extra cold-start per worker. Schedule rate-limited rollouts. :gear:

Vikram: Also add a fallback policy to route to a higher-precision replica if latency/quality breaches. That should keep customer-facing SLOs intact.

Maya: Long-term refactor idea: unify kernel selection, model metadata, and runtime profile in a single 'serving manifest'. That manifest drives compilation, cache layout, and rollout strategy. Would let us reason about compatibility and provide atomic profile swaps.

Jenn: Sounds good. Action items: 1) Maya to update RFC with profile config proto + cache header idea. 2) Vikram to sketch runtime adapter (tiers + fallback). 3) Diego to prototype Optimize integration for recommendations. 4) Jenn to define eval thresholds and CI gating.

Maya: I'll push an updated RFC draft this afternoon. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Vikram: Thanks. I'll prototype a minimal config parser and a fake cache header to simulate misses.

Diego: I'll wire a PoC in Optimize that runs offline quant sims and emits recommendation signals.

Jenn: I'll write the initial eval harness + a checklist for rollout gating.

SRE-Bot: Note: scheduled maintenance window tonight 02:00->03:00 UTC may affect canaries. Plan accordingly.
